2. The pre-emptor-opposite party filed Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 1978 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Bogra under Section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-empting the land measuring 1 '49 acres purchased by the petitioners at Taka 10,000/00 from one Abiran Bibi. 

 4. The learned Subordinate Judge allowed the pre-emption case of the pre-emptor-opposite party by his judgment and order dated 29-4-80. The present petitioners preferred a Miscellaneous Appeal No. 15 of 1981 in the Court of District Judge, Bogra, against the judgment and order dated 29-4-80 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and the same is now pending on transfer in the 1st Court of Additional District Judge, Bogra for disposal. On 7-8-81 the petitioners filed a petition praying for an adjournment of the hearing of the case and also filed the verified petition under Order 41 Rule 27(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure supported by an affidavit praying for recalling opposite party witness No.2 and for taking the documents as per list as additional evidence on the ground stated therein. The learned Additional District Judge hearing both the parties rejected the petition, however, the prayer for adjournment was allowed. Against that order the preemptees-petitioners filed an application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 6. Mr. A.T.M. Kamrul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party stated in his counter affidavit that when the purported certified copies of the rent receipts claimed to have been obtained by the petitioners through search in the collectorate are collusive and fraudulent documents created for the purpose of defeating the claim of pre-emption by the opposite party. The learned Advocate also submitted that the learned Additional District Judge rightly rejected the petitioners' application under Order 41 Rule 27(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and rightly held that the ground for additional evidence was not satisfactory.
